title: Ops vignettes — week of 2029-04-21: SRE handoff notes and SLO snapshots
content:
Quick context and purpose:
These are short operational vignettes for the on-call handoff and weekly SRE sync. Unpolished; notes-to-self style. Use the links above for traces and dashboards. If anything needs to be escalated to the platform/serving-runtime squad, tag the ticket with @serving-runtime.

TL;DR (1-liner each):
- Incident A: transient embeddings latency spike (~p99) caused by cold KV-cache behavior after a model rollout — mitigated by cache-warming and temporary routing to previous variant; follow-up: add bake window to rollout (INF-512).
- Incident B: single-node GPU OOM leading to 5–7min degradation for dedicated pool X; autoscaler didn’t replace fast enough; follow-up: tune replacement threshold and add node health probe (INF-513).
- Ops housekeeping: start-of-week handoff checklist refined; add prefix cache warmers to canary job and surface warm-up metrics in Console.

Vignette A — embeddings-route latency spike (2029-04-22 03:14–03:48 UTC)
- What happened: After a minor model variant rollout to hosted-api model catalog (model v3.2-q8 -> v3.3-q8), we saw an increase in p99 latency on /embeddings (-text) route. P95 stable, p99 moved from ~220ms to ~1.2s for a ~30min window.
- Root cause hypothesis: The new variant changes KV key layout and invalidated prefix cache + LRU churn in the shared KV cache tier. Cold-cache requests hit a slower code path that did additional per-token tensor prep (CPU fallback) before GPU op.
- Impact: Few customer requests timed out on high-concurrency jobs; overall error rate stayed <0.05% but latency SLO worried. No committed SLA breaches yet, but error budget consumption spiked in the p99 slice.
- Mitigation steps taken: 1) Rollback routing for new variant to warm pool; 2) kicked off a cache-warm job that replayed representative prefix traces for 10 minutes; 3) enabled temporary increased concurrency throttle to reduce simultaneous cold-joins.
- Follow-ups / action items:
  * INF-512 (owner: Ravi) — Add explicit bake window to model rollout process and a pre-rollout cache-warm job.
  * Add a metric for "cold prefix hits" and make it a Console tile (owner: Aisha).
  * Write small spec for KV key stability guarantees during minor model updates (owner: Maya).

Vignette B — dedicated pool X node OOM and slow replace (2029-04-23 11:02 UTC)
- What happened: One node in dedicated GPU pool-nyc-2 returned periodic OOMs under normal load (background quantization job). Node became unhealthy but the autoscaler replaced it only after ~6 minutes because the current replacement safety window is conservative. During that window, queue depths increased and tail latency rose.
- Root cause: two contributing factors — (1) background maintenance job not isolated from inference processes, (2) autoscaler health threshold is set to 4 consecutive failed probes with 30s probe interval.
- Impact: tail latency (p99) for dedicated customers using pool X increased from 320ms to 820ms, some requests queued and retried, one customer opened a support ticket (CS-880).
- Mitigation: temporarily cordoned the node, cancelled/paused the maintenance job, and manually triggered replacement. Confirmed subsequent node replacement finished in ~90s.
- Follow-ups / action items:
  * INF-513 (owner: Liam) — reduce autoscaler replacement threshold (from 4->2 failures) and decrease probe interval (30s->15s) for dedicated pools. Run a risk review with SRE + infra.
  * Add isolation policy so maintenance/quant jobs are throttled away from inference pods in high-util pools.
  * CS follow-up: prepare customer note explaining impact and mitigation (owner: Maya, liaise with customer-success).

SLO snapshot and trend notes (week-of-Apr-21):
- Target SLOs: hosted text generation p99 <= 450ms; embeddings p99 <= 350ms; dedicated p99 <= 400ms. Error-rate SLO: 0.5% per-week.
- This week (rolling 7d):
  * hosted text gen p99: 462ms (slightly above SLO)
  * embeddings p99: 518ms (above SLO; see Vignette A)
  * dedicated p99: 385ms (within SLO but with noticeable spikes tied to node replacement events)
  * error rate: 0.41% (within SLO but trending up during incidents)
- Notes: embeddings p99 is the main red flag — burns error budget and needs both operational fixes (warmers, rollout bake) and a perf regression guard in the model onboarding pipeline.

Handoff checklist (for incoming on-call):
- Quick state: watch embeddings p99 tile and cold-prefix metric; track INF-512/INF-513 progress.
- Current active pages: one open customer ticket (CS-880), two active infra alerts (dedicated pool health and autoscaler retries).
- Pager rotation: Maya -> Ravi -> Liam (this week).
- Escalation path: if dedicated pool replacement > 5 minutes, escalate to infra lead (@A. Chen). If embeddings variance persists after 2 bake attempts, halt rollout and notify product-hosted-api.
- Immediate runbook pointers:
  * For warm-cache issues: run warm-job from /ops/scripts/cache-warm-replay.sh, then validate cold-prefix metric falls by >90% in 10m.
  * For OOM/replace delays: cordon node, call manual replacement, check autoscaler logs under /var/log/autoscaler.

Operational improvements proposed (short items):
- Add a small canary-run after each catalog model update that simulates prefix diversity (owner: Maya, INF-514).
- Expose "warm-up success" boolean in rollout API response so Rollouts UI can show status (owner: product-hosted-api).
- Create a dedicated maintenance-window policy that prevents heavy background jobs on pools serving live traffic (owner: infra).

Meeting notes (SRE sync, 2029-04-23):
- Discussed INF-512 and INF-513, prioritized both for this sprint; agreed on low-risk autoscaler tuning with a rollback plan.
- Agreed to make cold-prefix metric part of weekly SLO digest (start next Monday).
- Proposed a 1-hour brown-bag next week on 'cache warming strategies' for devs and solutions engineers — tentatively May 2, 2029.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Do we add a permanent cache warming agent to Dedicated pools? Pros: faster warm-ups post-rollout; cons: more background load and management.
- Should we instrument model onboarding to require a micro-benchmark for KV-key stability? (product-hosted-api to weigh in)

Action items summary (owners and rough ETA):
- INF-512 (Ravi) — rollout bake + cache warm job, ETA: 2029-04-30.
- INF-513 (Liam) — autoscaler probe tuning + risk review, ETA: 2029-04-29.
- Console tile for cold-prefix (Aisha) — ETA: 2029-05-03.
- Customer note for CS-880 (Maya + CS) — draft by 2029-04-24.

Notes to incoming on-call:
- Try not to escalate rollouts immediately — prefer short rollback + bake unless errors exceed 0.2% in a 15m window.
- Keep an eye on the new cold-prefix metric (it should go to near-zero after a successful warm).
- If you need a quick trace link, use confluence:ops/slo-dashboard -> embeddings -> trace-sampler (search for traces around 03:15 UTC).

End of notes.

(rough scratch below — internal timings, trace ids, and quick commands)
- trace ids seen in incident A: trace-7ff3a, trace-88b9c
- quick commands: kubectl -n dedicated get pods -l pool=nyc-2; /ops/scripts/cache-warm-replay.sh --model v3.2-q8 --duration 600

Maya Chen
SRE — Redwood Inference
